title.narrative: 72nd International Federation of Medical Students Associations (IFMSA) March Meeting General Assembly in Estonia

description.narrative: The IFMSA August meeting is one of the biggest youth-led events with more than 1000 delegates from all over the world. It takes place twice a year to engage youth in matters of global health. It features training, workshops, and serves as a network platform for students worldwide to learn, discuss, network, and exchange knowledge. MEDSAR and IMCC are all members of IFMSA. In 2020, the March Meeting General Assembly that took place physically was hosted by MEDSAR here at Kigali and when COVID-19 broke out, IFMSA adopted the online settings for its most activities including the General assemblies. As IFMSA settled the path to its recovery, March Meeting General assembly 2022 hosted in a hybrid format where maximum members’ engaged and their involved in decision making and shaping IFMSA’s future were convened in North Macedonia. Following this March meeting, we are glad that MEDSAR delegates have even participated in 71st August meeting 2022 that took place in Turkey. During the network activity, we aim to strengthen our organizational skills and capacity on COVID-19 recovery, networking, and meeting our different partners including IMCC. In addition, we will present the outcomes of our recently finalized project, “Green group and partners’ SDG Seminar” as well as get to learn from activities and projects conducted by other National Member organizations(NMOs) with networking and knowledge exchange. At the end of this networking activity, we will gain the knowledge to sustain our organization, strengthen our current partnership project (Youth Education Activities on Sexual and Reproductive Health project, YEASRH) and share the experience gained with the rest of the medical students in our organization. We will also acquire skills and experience to host our upcoming international and local events, namely MEDSAR Day 2023, Africa regional meeting 2023 and SCOPE exchanges amidst the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.
